cards.explanation: The answer is the house of the LORD. Hezekiah tears his clothes, puts on sackcloth, and walks straight into the house of the LORD (2 Kings 19:1). Bad news lands, and he heads for the LORD's house. Some of us head for the fridge, friends, but I only deal in cookies.

The answer is Isaiah son of Amoz. Hezekiah sends Eliakim, Shebna and the leading priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah (2 Kings 19:2). That's a whole delegation heading to one prophet.
The answer is prayer. Hezekiah says, "Therefore lift up a prayer for the remnant that still survives." (2 Kings 19:4) He asks the prophet to pray for the people who are still left.

The answer is land. The LORD says Sennacherib will hear a rumor and "…return to his own land, where I will cause him to fall by the sword." (2 Kings 19:7) The LORD even says what happens to him once he's there.

The answer is False. Sennacherib hears Tirhakah, king of Cush, has set out to fight him, and he still sends messengers to Hezekiah again (2 Kings 19:9). He hears about Tirhakah and still sends more words to Jerusalem. Some folks just can't leave a letter unsent, friends.

The answer is True. That's his whole point. He tells Hezekiah, "Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying that Jerusalem will not be delivered into the hand of the king of Assyria." (2 Kings 19:10) Then he lists the nations and their gods, as if they all lost, so Hezekiah's God will lose too.

The answer is that he spreads it out before the LORD. Hezekiah read the letter, went up to the house of the LORD, and "…spread it out before the LORD." (2 Kings 19:14) He takes the whole threat and lays it right there in front of Him. The letter came through Sennacherib's messengers, and Hezekiah reads it before he takes it up.

The answer is True. Hezekiah prays, "O LORD, God of Israel, enthroned between the cherubim, You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth." (2 Kings 19:15) He's got the Maker of everything in front of him, and he says so first. That line comes right at the opening, before he asks for anything.

The answer is True. Hezekiah prays, "Truly, O LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste these nations and their lands." (2 Kings 19:17) He doesn't dodge the hard part. He names it out loud to the LORD.

The answer is that they were only wood and stone. Hezekiah says Assyria cast those gods into the fire "…for they were not gods, but only wood and stone—the work of human hands." (2 Kings 19:18) That's the reason he gives for why they were destroyed. Earlier in the same prayer he tells the LORD, "…You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth." (2 Kings 19:15)

The answer is so all kingdoms know the LORD alone is God. Hezekiah asks, "…please save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You alone, O LORD, are God." (2 Kings 19:19) He wants more than his own city safe. He wants the whole earth to know who the LORD is.

The answer is True. The LORD's word says, "The Virgin Daughter of Zion despises you and mocks you; the Daughter of Jerusalem shakes her head behind you." (2 Kings 19:21) Sennacherib had been taunting, and now the shaking head is aimed at him. It's the LORD's own word against him.

The answer is the Holy One of Israel. The LORD asks, "Whom have you taunted and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!" (2 Kings 19:22) The LORD answers His own question. So the one Sennacherib has been taunting is the Holy One of Israel, not another king.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "Long ago I ordained it; in days of old I planned it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should crush fortified cities into piles of rubble." (2 Kings 19:25) He says He ordained it long ago and has now brought it to pass. So the conquests weren't apart from His plan.

The answer is that the LORD will put a hook in his nose and send him back. He says, "…I will put My hook in your nose and My bit in your mouth; I will send you back the way you came." (2 Kings 19:28) The hook and bit are the LORD's picture of sending Sennacherib back. Later the text says he "…broke camp and withdrew." (2 Kings 19:36)

The answer is that they'll sow and reap again. The LORD says, "But in the third year you will sow and reap; you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit." (2 Kings 19:29) Two years of food that grows on its own, then a full planting season.

The answer is False. The LORD says the king of Assyria "…will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it." (2 Kings 19:32) He also says the king will not "…come before it with a shield or build up a siege ramp against it." (2 Kings 19:32) So not even one arrow, friends.

The answer is David. The LORD says, "I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David." (2 Kings 19:34) David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), is the servant He names.

The answer is back home to Nineveh. The text says, "So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there." (2 Kings 19:36) The LORD had said, "He will go back the way he came…" (2 Kings 19:33) Nineveh is where the text says he ends up. He went home, just as the LORD said.

The answer is Esar-haddon. After Adrammelech and Sharezer put their father to the sword, the text says, "And his son Esar-haddon reigned in his place." (2 Kings 19:37) The throne passes to a third son.
